measured_facts: Every train step runs 48 full-position readout CEs per microbatch, for separate heads (sep) and for probes (PLS_DETACH_BB=1) alike: per_layer_qwen3.py:613-619 (supervised) loops k=0..L-2 plus the final readout. train/pls/L{k} reuses the same CE values, so the train step recomputes no logits. pls_probe is off in these runs. The per-layer eval is a separate program and runs every 1000 steps (5 times per run).

FLOPs per token, checked from the code: one readout GEMM is 2*512*128256 = 131.3 MFLOP. The CE issues 4 GEMMs (forward, backward recompute, dX, dW), so 48 readouts cost 25.2 GFLOP/token (18.9 GFLOP/token with the usual 3x count). The body costs about 3 GFLOP/token: 6*182M params is 1.09 GFLOP, causal attention at seq 4096 is about 1.6 GFLOP, plus remat. Readouts are about 89% of FLOPs.

Step time against depth, median s/it from logs/slurm. Baseline with no readouts (FSDP, full microbatch): d12 1.0, d24 1.8, d36 2.5. Baseline d48 at PDP=4: 2.9 (logs/muonh-qwen3-130m-della4xh100-d48-diag600-pdp4.log.log). PDP=4 designs at d48 with readouts: sandwich, preln, lns, keel, deepnorm sep 15.1-15.4, probes 15.0-15.4. So the 47 extra readouts cost 12.3 s, which is 81% of the step, or 0.262 s per readout per step. That is about 263 TFLOP/s per GPU, 27% of bf16 peak.

HC at microbatch 1 (PDP=1), sep/probes: d12 6.5/6.3, d24 12.7/12.5, d48 25.4/25.0 s/it. A linear fit gives 0.522 s per layer (body plus one readout) and about 0.1 s fixed cost. Other PDP=1 designs at d48: mhc 25.8/25.6, mhcid 24.4, attnres 34.4-34.7, attnres_block 24.0, moda 43.0-43.4, hc-static 24.5, attnres-static 31.0, arqclip 34.4-34.6. The 6-layer sep runs take 1.7-1.8 s/it.

Temp-size test 15322826 (logs/pls_depth_controls.yaml:182-184). Microbatch 4: hc 16.0 s/step and 32.91 GiB temp, mhc 16.2 s and 33.07 GiB, lns 15.2 s and 30.61 GiB, attnres 32.5 s and 53.36 GiB. Microbatch 1: mhc 25.3 s and 17.69 GiB. Microbatch 2: every design OOM at 107-128 GiB. So at the same depth, PDP=1 costs hc and mhc +58% step time against PDP=4. For attnres it costs +6%.

The CE path depends on PDP. PDP=4 (16384 tokens per device per microbatch) takes batched_xla's H100 b-tiled path (batched_xla.py:369-389, 432-442): full-vocab f32 logits [8192,128256] per block, and a backward with bf16 dlogits plus a scatter (batched_xla.py:603). PDP=1 (4096 tokens) fails the shared-memory guard in batched_xla (h512 x v1024 x 2B = 1 MiB > 101 KB, batched_xla.py:192-200, logged as a RuntimeWarning in arch3-hc-d24-sep_w80_train.log:553). It then falls back to the 'xla' path with v_block 8192 and b_block 4096. The forward of that batched_xla path is pure XLA, so the Triton guard no longer applies to it.

The 'xla' fallback that PDP=1 runs use has a slow backward (fast_backward default False, xla.py:36). CPU StableHLO shows both backward GEMMs with f32 operands: (f32[4096,8192] x f32[512,8192]) and (f32[4096,512] x f32[4096,8192]). On H100 these run as FP32/TF32, not bf16 tensor cores. The backward also has a scatter-add, and it accumulates grad_x in bf16 across the 16 vocab blocks (xla.py:319). LEVANTER_CE_XLA_FAST_BWD=1 switches it to bf16 GEMMs, a one-hot label term and a scan (CPU HLO: bf16 dot operands, no scatter).

CE numerics on CPU at B=1024, H=512, V=128256, against a float32 reference (scratch: /scratch/gpfs/GROUP/USER/tmp/pls_speed/readout/ce_numerics.py). The loss is bitwise identical on all paths. xla_slow (what PDP=1 runs use): grad_x rel err 5.3e-3, grad_w 1.4e-5. xla_fast and btiled (what PDP=4 runs use): grad_x 7.6e-4, grad_w 3.9e-4. So PDP=1 designs (hc, mhc, attnres, moda) and PDP=4 designs (preln, sandwich, lns, ...) train with two different CE backward numerics today. btiled with the scatter replaced by a one-hot is bitwise equal to btiled in loss, grad_x and grad_w.

Probe runs still run the dX GEMM. The readout norm scale (aux_norms) is trainable, so x = norm(stop_gradient(h)) still carries a gradient. CPU HLO (c4_dots.py) shows 4 GEMMs including f32[8192,512] = dX. With the scale folded into the head, XLA drops it and 3 remain. This explains why probes are only 0.1-0.4 s/step faster than sep. Removing dX should save at least 0.8 s/step at bf16 peak.

Communication under PARAM_MAP=vocab, from a CPU 4-device compile of the real gradient path (comm_hlo.py; levanter microbatched, mp p=f32,c=bf16, launcher mesh). The all-gather of the f32 [128256,512] heads is hoisted out of the microbatch loop and runs once per step. Inside the loop, every microbatch all-reduces the full f32 [512,128256] gradient of every head. At 48 heads that is 12.6 GB per microbatch, 32 times per step at PDP=1 and 8 times at PDP=4. On GPU this probably becomes a reduce-scatter of 9.45 GB per GPU: about 0.84 s/step at PDP=1 if not overlapped (inferred, not measured).

Memory inference: per-head copies explain most of the GPU temp buffer. A gathered bf16 head (131 MB) plus its full f32 gradient (263 MB) is 394 MB, and 48 of them make 17.6 GiB. That matches the 17.69 GiB measured at PDP=1. Adding the b-tiled logits, dlogits f32 and bf16 buffers (about 9.8 GiB) gives about 30 GiB at PDP=4, which matches 30.6-32.9 GiB. On CPU the temp grows by 0.85 GB per head (L=5: 4.22 GB, L=9: 7.62 GB).

LEVANTER_PALLAS_CE_AUTOTUNE_ON_MISS=0 is correct to keep. The PDP=4 b-tiled path ignores block sizes completely (b_block 8192 is hard-coded, no vocab tiling), so the 7-candidate sweep would only waste time. At PDP=1, every batched_xla candidate with v_block >= 128 fails the guard, and v_block 64 passes it. That would produce a Python-unrolled forward over about 2000 vocab blocks. On the 'xla' path the block size changes more than tiling: v_block sets how many bf16 grad_x accumulations happen (rounding) and the order of the LSE logaddexp.

Per-layer eval takes 9.0 min at PDP=4 (909 batches of 16, 1.7 it/s) and 13.5 min at PDP=1 (3630 batches of 4, 4.5 it/s), 5 times per run. That is 3.5% of a preln run and 3.2% of an hc run. The main eval (one readout) takes 2 min and duplicates eval/L47 within 1e-4 to 5e-4 (smoke gate).

Roofline model for the PDP=4 b-tiled readout, per token per readout: forward about 1.54 MB of HBM traffic (f32 logits written, then read twice for logsumexp). Backward about 2.82 MB: f32 logits written, the exp/mul fusion reads them and writes f32 dlogits, the scatter runs in place, a convert reads f32 and writes bf16, and the two GEMMs read bf16. In total 27 TB per GPU per step, about 9 s at 3 TB/s, plus about 4.7 s of GEMMs. That predicts about 15 s/step against the measured 15.2 s, so the readouts are memory-bound on f32 logits traffic.

The CE input therefore depends on g, and the CE backward still needs dX to get dg. The proposer's c4_dots.py on the b-tiled path shows 4 GEMMs drop to 3 when g is folded into W. The small probe/sep gap (0.1-0.4 s) fits a dX GEMM that still runs. Keep x=bf16(g*n) and W as they are, and wrap them in a custom_vjp whose backward runs the CE backward, keeps only gw (gx becomes dead, so XLA drops the dX GEMM through the loop-carry DCE already seen on CPU), and returns dg_j = sum_v W_jv*gw_jv / g_j, with f32 accumulation and a guard for |g_j| near 0. candidates.title: Faster checkpoint staging: device-to-host through pinned memory or concurrent transfers instead of the pageable bounce path

candidates.mechanism: The save is async in design: after staging, the commits drain in a background thread. But staging blocks the loop and runs at only 1.65-2.7 GiB/s. Staging copies each shard into pageable CPU memory via jax.device_put(unpinned_host) and then np.array(copy=True) inside one asyncio thread. So raising max_staged_host_bytes would NOT help. Staging via pinned_host, or copy_to_host_async on all shards before any materialization, could reach PCIe speed (about 10+ GiB/s per GPU).
candidates.saving_basis: If staging drops from 20.5 s to about 3-5 s per save: 2.5% of wall alone (hc d48: 199 saves x 16 s = 53 min of 37 h), or about 0.8% on top of C2. Speculative: the attainable pinned D2H rate on these nodes is not measured.

(1) gemm_fusion_dot_general.814 writes the logits as bf16[8192,128256]: the dot has no preferred_element_type, so the logits are already bf16 and are only upcast after. (2) loop_multiply_fusion reads them and writes f32 dlogits[8192,128256], 4.2 GB. (3) input_scatter_fusion updates that buffer in place. (4) wrapped_convert.42 reads the 4.2 GB f32 and writes 2.1 GB bf16. (5) The two GEMMs read the bf16. A select variant becomes one fusion: read 2.1 GB, write 2.1 GB bf16. Traffic falls from 12.6 GB to 4.2 GB, 8.4 GB less per block, as claimed (the claim's reason, f32 logits, was wrong). Recomputed: preln d48 PDP=4 runs 8 microbatches of 2 blocks each, so 48 readouts x 16 blocks x 8.4 GB = 6.45 TB per step. At 2.8-3.0 TB/s that is 2.2-2.3 s of 15.1 s/it, at most 15%. I give 10% because elementwise passes rarely reach peak bandwidth and the step-level gain is unmeasured. The saving applies only to PDP>=2 runs (preln, lns, gilns d48 and larger sizes). hc, mhc, attnres, attnres_block and moda run at B=4096 per device, below _H100_FULL_VOCAB_B_TILED_MIN_BATCH=8192. They take the xla.py streaming fallback and get 0%, and their compiled programs should not change. Numerics: the CPU test (onehot_test.py) is bitwise for grad_x and grad_w. In w16 (hc) the step was lowered at 00:21:25, the stuck warning came at 00:22:17 and the abort at 00:22:57, and a single local device thread never arrived. Width changes also change the data-parallel and vocab-shard reduction order against the 4-GPU controls (summation-order class), and the launcher note about FSDP-sharded readouts that depend on the rest of the program shows this stack is sensitive to layout. Useful as a latency option only, and not a speed setup.
